edges.description: Null allele produces early severe loss of rods and cones.
edges.limitations: A null allele rather than the patient missense genotype, and an early, rapid degeneration in mice against a human course whose tempo is undocumented. Cone-first loss is not shown.

edges.description: The patient allele mislocalises in mouse RPE in vivo.
edges.limitations: Localisation was read from EGFP-tagged knock-in alleles, and in homozygotes rather than the patients' compound heterozygous genotype.

edges.description: Homozygous patient allele causes photoreceptor loss.
edges.limitations: Homozygous Phe350Cys, whereas patients were reported compound heterozygous with Asp345His; the compound genotype has no phenotype in mice. Degeneration is complete within weeks of birth.

edges.description: The human genotype does not reproduce retinal degeneration in mice.
edges.limitations: Mice live far shorter than humans and mouse and human Sema4A differ at a few residues, so a slowly progressive human disease or a species-specific effect of Asp345His could be missed.

nodes.description: Missense variants in the conserved sema domain of SEMA4A. p.Phe350Cys is the variant with functional support; in a structural model F350 sits in a hydrophobic pocket, and replacing it with a small residue is predicted to destabilise the fold. p.Asp345His is semi-conserved and causes no retinal disease when knocked in to mice. Semaphorin receptor binding is the canonical activity of SEMA4A and is bound here to name the protein's function; no modifier is given because the structural model places F350 far from the predicted plexin-binding surface, and the retinal defect is attributed to misfolding and loss of endosomal sorting rather than to lost receptor binding.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of novel mutations in the SEMA4A gene associated with retinal degenerative diseases.
evidence.snippet: Two mutations, p.D345H and p.F350C, were observed only in affected patients; they were not observed in any of the normal members or the 100 control subjects. Both mutations identified occur in the conserved semaphorin domain.

nodes.description: Progressive retinal dystrophy classified as cone-rod dystrophy in the patients of the original report. Age at onset, rate of progression and electroretinographic detail for SEMA4A cone-rod dystrophy have not been published.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of novel mutations in the SEMA4A gene associated with retinal degenerative diseases.
evidence.snippet: We report the first observation of the involvement of SEMA4A gene mutations causing retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and cone rod dystrophy (CRD).

nodes.description: In darkness Sema4A shuttles retinoid-binding proteins with their retinoids between the RPE cell surface and the ER, where 11-cis-retinal is regenerated and returned to photoreceptors. Loss of this sorting impairs chromophore supply for phototransduction.
nodes.id: Impaired Retinoid-Binding Protein Sorting for the Visual Cycle

evidence.reference_title: Endosomal sorting by Semaphorin 4A in retinal pigment epithelium supports photoreceptor survival.
evidence.snippet: In the absence of oxidative stress, Sema4A sorts retinoid-binding proteins with retinoids between the cell surface and endoplasmic reticulum, by which 11-cis-retinal, a chromophore for phototransduction, is regenerated and transported back to photoreceptors.

nodes.description: In RPE cells Sema4A acts as an intracellular sorting factor in the Rab11/FIP2 endosomal pathway rather than as an extracellular guidance cue. It directs two cargoes: prosaposin, which it diverts from the lysosome to exosomal release under oxidative stress, and retinoid-binding proteins such as CRALBP, which it carries between the ER and the cell surface for the visual cycle.
nodes.id: Impaired Sema4A-Dependent Endosomal Sorting in RPE

evidence.reference_title: Endosomal sorting by Semaphorin 4A in retinal pigment epithelium supports photoreceptor survival.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that Semaphorin 4A (Sema4A), a member of axonal guidance molecule semaphorin, plays a role in Rab11/FIP2-mediated endosomal sorting in retinal pigment epithelial cells to support photoreceptor function.

nodes.description: No disease-modifying treatment exists. Management is the supportive care common to inherited retinal dystrophies: low-vision aids, filtered lenses, periodic ophthalmological follow-up, and genetic counseling. No source specific to SEMA4A disease was found.

Loss of rod and cone photoreceptors and thinning of the outer nuclear layer. In mice it begins as abnormal outer segment formation during the period when outer segments meet the RPE microvilli and is severe within weeks. Whether cones are lost before rods in the human disease, as the disease name implies, has not been documented beyond the original clinical classification.

nodes.description: Overexpressed Asp345His and Phe350Cys proteins increase the ER stress marker GRP78 after light exposure, sensitise RPE cells to ER and oxidative stress, and suppress phagocytosis. This is an overexpression finding in a cell line; whether it contributes to photoreceptor loss in vivo has not been tested, so no edge to photoreceptor degeneration is asserted.

evidence.reference_title: SEMA4A mutations lead to susceptibility to light irradiation, oxidative stress, and ER stress in retinal pigment epithelial cells.
evidence.snippet: The expression of GRP78 was increased by mutant SEMA4A following light irradiation, and phagocytosis was suppressed in mutant SEMA4A-transfected cells. Mutant SEMA4A induced susceptibility to ER stress and oxidative stress.

nodes.description: Under light-induced oxidative stress, Sema4A switches prosaposin from the lysosomal route to exosomal release, and the secreted prosaposin protects photoreceptors from apoptosis. Without functional Sema4A this protective release falls.
nodes.id: Reduced Exosomal Prosaposin Release from RPE

evidence.reference_title: Endosomal sorting by Semaphorin 4A in retinal pigment epithelium supports photoreceptor survival.
evidence.snippet: In response to oxidative stress, Sema4A switches the endosomal sorting of the lysosomal precursor protein prosaposin from the lysosome to the exosomal release, which prevents light-induced photoreceptor apoptosis.

nodes.description: Loss of central acuity is the usual first symptom of cone and cone-rod dystrophies. It is listed in the OMIM summary for this disease but has no citable primary report for SEMA4A; the evidence is the description of the disease class.

evidence.snippet: Characteristic symptoms include decreasing visual acuity, reading difficulties, photophobia and dyschromatopsia.

nodes.description: Sema4A normally sits at the apical plasma membrane of RPE cells. The Phe350Cys protein forms high-molecular-weight aggregates and is retained intracellularly; one overexpression study placed the retained mutant protein in the endoplasmic reticulum. That study also found Asp345His retained in the ER of ARPE-19 cells, whereas in knock-in mouse RPE and in the knock-in study's own ARPE-19 and COS-7 assays Asp345His reached the cell surface, so the Asp345His localisation defect is assay-dependent.

nodes.description: Knock-in of the patient Phe350Cys allele disrupts photoreceptor outer segments by two weeks of age and removes photoreceptors by four weeks, matching the null phenotype. Heterozygotes are normal.

Mice lacking Sema4a from a gene-trap insertion have severe retinal degeneration with attenuated vessels and depigmentation by 14 weeks, an outer nuclear layer reduced to a single row, and impaired rod and cone function.

Lentiviral delivery of wild-type Sema4a to the subretinal space of Sema4a-null and Phe350Cys knock-in mice preserved the photoreceptor layer for at least four months and partly restored ERG responses. This is a preclinical result only; no human trial was found.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, Sema4A gene transfer successfully prevents photoreceptor degeneration in Sema4A(F350C/F350C) and Sema4A(-/-) mice.

nodes.description: Cytoplasmic-tail variant originally reported as dominant. It does not segregate with retinal disease, occurs homozygous in an unaffected relative, and causes no phenotype in homozygous knock-in mice; it is not disease-causing and is listed only to record that.

evidence.snippet: The p.R713Q variant in SEMA4A is insufficient to cause either autosomal recessive or autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa and is unlikely to be pathogenic.
